title: Patch: a card opened from the patch notes shows its loading and retry states instead of nothing
thread:
**Issue #2052 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #2052: Patch: a card opened from the patch notes shows its loading and retry states instead of nothing Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means On the patch-notes page, clicking a card's name in a "changed in this patch" list opens that card's detail. On a slow connection the click looks dead — nothing appears while the card's data loads — and if the load fails, nothing ever appears and there is no retry. After this patch the click shows a loading state, and a failed load shows the error with a working Try again, the way every other panel on the same page already behaves. ## Why `OpenedCard` (`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx:331-336`) returns `null` for every non-ready `useLoaded` state. It is the only one of the file's five `useLoaded` consumers that swallows those states: `PatchCardsPanel` (`:195-213`), the top-level `PatchNotes` (`:459-484`) and `CardHistoryBody` (`patches/CardHistory.tsx:58-76`) all render loading, error and retry. The machinery is already there — `useLoaded` exposes `retry()` (`patches/context.tsx:57-64`) and failed loads are evicted so retry can succeed (`source.ts:114-117`). Distinct from issue #2036's listed items (skeletons, undo toasts, command menu, sheet gestures). ## Proposal Render the file's existing `patch-status`/`patch-retry` pattern inside `OpenedCard` for the `loading` and `error` states. ## Where it lands `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx` and its test. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A pending card open shows a loading line where the card will appear - [ ] A failed open shows the error sentence and a Try again that retries - [ ] A successful open is unchanged ## Size and risks Small: about twenty lines plus a test, reusing the file's own components. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40988979761)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal A card opened from the Patch notes page (`OpenedCard` in `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx`) shows its wait and its failure instead of nothing. A wait that lasts past `SKELETON_DELAY_MS` (300 ms) gets a loading line, "Loading this card…". A failed load gets "This card didn't load." and a Try again that retries. Both appear in a small dialog where the card's detail opens (the `inspect-detail` box, centred over a scrim), with Close, Escape, the scrim and Back closing it. A successful open is unchanged: a load that answers within 300 ms shows nothing first, and the detail opens exactly as today. ## Files to touch | Path | new/change | What | |---|---|---| | `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx` | change | imports; new component `OpeningCard`; `OpenedCard` renders it for `loading` (after the delay) and `error` | | `apps/web/src/patches/testids.ts` | change | five new keys in `patchTestid`: `opening`, `openingLoading`, `openingError`, `openingRetry`, `openingClose` | | `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` | change | two entries: `"Loading this card…"`, `"This card didn't load."` | | `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx` | change | three new tests in `describe("R388 the Patch notes page", …)` | Do not touch: `crates/`, `spec/` (no new ruling: this is presentation and decides no rule), `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/*` (it is reused as it is), `apps/web/src/skeleton/*`, `apps/web/src/patches/context.tsx`, `source.ts`, `CardHistory.tsx`, `patches.css`, `e2e/`, and every path in the bot's forbidden list. Governing notes: - R388: a card's name opens it in the detail view with its history. - R2115000 and R2108000: a menu's wait is a skeleton that never flashes. But R2108000's "What stays text" names "Dialogs, popovers, overlays", so this dialog's wait is a text line, not a `Skeleton`. The no-flash rule is copied through `useShownAfterDelay`. - CLAUDE.md rule 7: the patch data is public, and nothing here enforces a rule. ## Steps 1. **`apps/web/src/patches/testids.ts`.** In `patchTestid`, right after the `openCard: "patch-open-card",` line, add: ```ts /** #2052: the dialog in the detail's place while a card opened from a patch loads, or after it failed. */ opening: "patch-opening", openingLoading: "patch-opening-loading", openingError: "patch-opening-error", openingRetry: "patch-opening-retry", openingClose: "patch-opening-close", ``` 2. **`apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.** Right after the line `"This patch's cards didn't load.": "本次更新的卡牌未能加载。",` add the two lines below. The `…` is the single character U+2026, as in the `t()` call. `i18n.test.ts` (R711000) fails on any `t()` literal without an entry. `"Try again"`, `"Close"` and `"Card"` already have entries. ```json "Loading this card…": "正在加载这张牌…", "This card didn't load.": "这张牌未能加载。", ``` 3. **`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx`, imports.** - Line 6 becomes `import { useId, useRef, useState, type ReactElement } from "react";`. Directly under it, with no blank line, add `import { createPortal } from "react-dom";`. HeroInspect.tsx orders these the same way. - After line 13 (`import { CardDetail } from "../cards/inspect/CardDetail.tsx";`) add `import { OVERLAY_ROOT_PROPS, useModalOverlay } from "../cards/inspect/store.ts";`. - Line 16 becomes `import { Skeleton, useShownAfterDelay } from "../skeleton/Skeleton.tsx";`. - `type Loaded` is already imported from `./context.tsx`. `inspect.css` already loads through `CardDetail`, so it needs no import. 4. **`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx`, new component `OpeningCard`.** Insert it directly above `function OpenedCard` (line 330). It copies HeroInspect.tsx's and CardDetail.tsx's modal shell (`createPortal` to `document.body`, `inspect-layer` plus `inspect-scrim`, `useModalOverlay` focusing Close). The status blocks copy `PatchCardsPanel`'s `patch-status`/`patch-retry` markup (`:201-211`) and CardHistory.tsx's `

` line (`:76`). Copy exactly: ```tsx /** * #2052: the detail's place while a card opened from a patch loads, or after it failed: its status line, * Try again when it failed, and Close. A dialog as the detail is (`useModalOverlay`), so Escape, the * scrim and Back close it too; a dialog's wait stays text (R2108000). */ function OpeningCard({ read, onClose }: { read: Exclude, { status: "ready" }>; onClose: () => void }): ReactElement { const closeButton = useRef(null); const modal = useModalOverlay(onClose, closeButton); return createPortal(

{read.status === "loading" ? (

{t("Loading this card…")}

) : (

{t("This card didn't load.")}

)}
, document.body, ); } ``` 5. **`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx`, `OpenedCard`.** Keep its signature and its `source`/`read` lines. Replace the two lines from `if (read.status !== "ready" …` to the `return ` line with: ```tsx // #2052, R2108000: a card that answers within SKELETON_DELAY_MS opens as it always did, with no wait shown. const waited = useShownAfterDelay(); if (read.status === "ready") return read.value === null ? null : ; if (read.status === "loading" && !waited) return null; return ; ``` The hook call must sit above the first `return` (rules of hooks). `PatchList` already keys `OpenedCard` by `openId`, so each card's delay starts at its click. Change nothing in `PatchList`. 6. Run the tests and checks below. ## Tests In `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`, add three `it`s inside `describe("R388 the Patch notes page", …)`, right after `it("R388 a patch whose snapshot fails to load says so and tries again", …)` (ends at line 234). They use the file's own helpers (`renderPage`, `byCard`, `fixtureSource`) and existing imports (`INSPECT_DETAIL`, `vi`, `within`, `fireEvent`, `screen`), so the file needs no new import. Nothing on the page calls `source.index()` before a card opens, so overriding `index` reaches only the open, and then `CardHistory`. 1. `it("#2052 a card still loading shows its loading line where its detail opens, then the detail", async () => { … })`: - `const source = fixtureSource(); const index = source.index;` - Make a held promise: `let release = (): void => undefined; const held = new Promise((resolve) => { release = () => { resolve(); }; });` - `renderPage({ ...source, index: () => held.then(() => index()) });` then `await screen.findByTestId(patchTestid.cards);` - `fireEvent.click(within(byCard(patchTestid.changedCard, "core-002")).getByTestId(patchTestid.openCard));` - Right after the click: `expect(screen.queryByTestId(patchTestid.opening)).toBeNull();`. No flash inside the delay. - `const loading = await screen.findByTestId(patchTestid.openingLoading);` (it shows after 300 ms, within findBy's default 1000 ms). Assert it has the text content `"Loading this card…"` and `role` `"status"`. Assert `screen.getByTestId(patchTestid.opening)` has `role` `"dialog"`, and `screen.queryByTestId(INSPECT_DETAIL)` is null. - `release();` then `const detail = await screen.findByTestId(INSPECT_DETAIL);`. Assert `detail` has `data-card` `"core-002"`, and `screen.queryByTestId(patchTestid.opening)` is null. 2. `it("#2052 a card that fails to open says so where its detail would be, and Try again opens it", async () => { … })`. Copy the failure pattern of the test at `:221-234`: - `const source = fixtureSource(); let failures = 1; const index = source.index;` - `const quiet = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => undefined);` - `renderPage({ ...source, index: () => (failures-- > 0 ? Promise.reject(new Error("offline")) : index()) });`, then await `patchTestid.cards` and click core-002's name as in test 1. - `const error = await screen.findByTestId(patchTestid.openingError);`. Assert the text content `"This card didn't load."` and `role` `"alert"`. Assert `screen.queryByTestId(INSPECT_DETAIL)` is null. - `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId(patchTestid.openingRetry));` then `await screen.findByTestId(INSPECT_DETAIL)`. Assert its `data-card` is `"core-002"` and `screen.queryByTestId(patchTestid.opening)` is null. Then `quiet.mockRestore();`. 3. `it("#2052 a card that fails to open closes on Close and gives focus back to its name", async () => { … })`: - `index: () => Promise.reject(new Error("offline"))` on every call, with console.error quieted as in test 2. - `const name = within(byCard(patchTestid.changedCard, "core-002")).getByTestId(patchTestid.openCard); name.focus(); fireEvent.click(name);` - `await screen.findByTestId(patchTestid.openingError);` then assert `screen.getByTestId(patchTestid.openingClose)` has focus. - `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId(patchTestid.openingClose));` then assert `screen.queryByTestId(patchTestid.opening)` is null and `name` has focus. Then `quiet.mockRestore();`. The existing `it("R388 a card's name opens it as it stands now, …")` (`:173-187`) is the proof that a successful open is unchanged. It must still pass untouched. Commands (wasm first, since the web tests need it): ``` sh scripts/build-wasm.sh pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts src/patches/CardHistory.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/patches apps/web/src/i18n cargo jackioh spec check ``` ## Done when - [ ] A pending open that outlasts 300 ms shows "Loading this card…" in a dialog where the detail opens (test 1). - [ ] A failed open shows "This card didn't load." and a Try again that opens the card (test 2). Close closes it and gives focus back (test 3). - [ ] A successful open is unchanged: the existing R388 open test passes, and test 1 sees no dialog right after the click. - [ ] `PatchNotes.test.tsx`, `i18n.test.ts` and `CardHistory.test.tsx` pass. The web typecheck, eslint and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass. - [ ] The harness's checks pass (rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests). None of them is touched by this change, so a red one is reported by name, never hidden. ## Risks - **Focus.** `OpeningCard` takes focus to its Close. When the load succeeds, its unmount gives focus back to the name before `CardDetail` mounts and takes it. React runs a deleted component's layout cleanups before new layout effects. So the R388 test's final `expect(name).toHaveFocus()` still holds. Do not register `OpeningCard` with `registerDetail`: only a real detail takes the inspect slot. - **Back layers (R2127000).** `useModalOverlay` calls `useBackLayer`. A layer closed by unmount leaves its history entry spent, and `CardDetail`'s layer reuses it (`net/backLayers.ts` header), so the hand-over pushes no extra entry. - **A quick retry blinks.** A Try again pressed within 300 ms of the click shows nothing until the reload answers, because the delay has not passed yet. A person reads the error before pressing, so this is accepted rather than adding state. - **i18n.** Each new `t()` literal needs its `zh-CN.json` entry with the same `…` character, or `i18n.test.ts` fails. - **Rulings.** Test titles use `#2052`, not an R-id. The only R-id the new code cites is R2108000, which exists, so `spec check` stays green. Add no ruling note. - **Hidden information.** None: patch data is public (§5.1). ## Open questions None block the build. Decisions taken, with what was rejected: - **Where the wait shows.** It shows in a dialog in the detail's place, over a scrim. Rejected: the inline `patch-status` where `OpenedCard` sits today. That sits after every release line, a screen or more below the clicked name on the real page, so the click would still look dead. - **Loading line vs skeleton.** It is a text line, not a `Skeleton`. R2108000 keeps dialogs' waits as text. - **No flash.** The 300 ms delay (`useShownAfterDelay`) applies to the loading line only, so a fast open is exactly today's. The error shows at once. - **Card in no snapshot.** A card found in no snapshot (`read.value === null`) still renders nothing, as today. The issue does not ask about it. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-10-28T12:51:17Z: Approve ````
